name: hmm_regime_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, intraday microstructure alternates between trending micro-sessions — when institutional TWAP/VWAP algorithms are executing large directional orders — and mean-reverting periods dominated by market makers and liquidity providers absorbing order flow. This alternation is detectable in the sign autocorrelation of 5-second returns: during institutional execution windows, consecutive 5s bars trend in the same direction (directional consistency > 60% over 3 minutes), while market-maker-dominated periods show near-random or negatively autocorrelated returns (consistency < 42%). In trending regime, we follow the institutional direction using 2-min/6-min EMA alignment; in mean-reverting regime, we fade z-score extremes as market makers push price back toward the intraday mean within 30-60 seconds.

indicators.name: dir_consistency_36
indicators.formula: fraction of consecutive-bar pairs with same return sign over 36-bar rolling window
indicators.purpose: 36 bars (3 min) is the minimum window to distinguish institutional execution bursts from random noise at 5s resolution. Shorter windows (< 24 bars) produce too many false regime flips; longer windows (> 60 bars) lag genuine regime transitions. 3 min matches typical TWAP algorithm slice intervals. This is NOT 12x the original — the original used full Viterbi decoding over an entire prior session; here we use a rolling local measure calibrated to the hold time of 30-90s.

indicators.name: ema_24
indicators.purpose: 2-min fast EMA (24 × 5s) captures the current directional push within a trending regime. Original used EMA(9) on 1-min bars = 9-min context; compressed to 2-min because we hold 30-90s and need a trigger-level signal, not a context filter. 2-min EMA reacts fast enough to confirm in-progress institutional flow.

indicators.name: ema_72
indicators.purpose: 6-min slow EMA (72 × 5s) provides trend direction context within the trending regime. Original used EMA(21) on 1-min = 21-min context; compressed to 6-min because trending micro-sessions on NIFTY last 5-15 min, not 20+ min. The 2-min/6-min pair gives 1:3 fast/slow ratio, same as the original's 9:21.

indicators.name: zscore_60
indicators.purpose: 5-min rolling z-score (60 × 5s) for mean-reversion entry signal. Replaces Bollinger Bands (original used SMA(20) on 1-min = 20-min window) because 5-min captures enough intraday mean to identify short-term deviations relevant to 30-90s reversion trades. Longer windows (120+ bars) mix different intraday regimes; shorter (< 36 bars) produce too-frequent extremes.

conditions: TRENDING: dir_consistency_36 > trend_threshold (0.60) AND ema_24 > ema_72 by > ema_signal_threshold (0.03%) AND last 5s return > 0 — institutional flow is pushing up, enter with it
REVERTING: dir_consistency_36 < reversion_threshold (0.42) AND zscore_60 < -1.5 — price has overshot the 5-min mean to the downside; market makers will fade it back up within 30-60s
TRENDING: dir_consistency_36 > trend_threshold (0.60) AND ema_24 < ema_72 by > ema_signal_threshold (0.03%) AND last 5s return < 0 — institutional selling is sustained, follow down
REVERTING: dir_consistency_36 < reversion_threshold (0.42) AND zscore_60 > 1.5 — price has overshot above 5-min mean; market makers will push it back down

exit.stop_rationale: Trending regime: 4 option pts = ~8 spot pts. NIFTY trending micro-sessions should not retrace more than 8 spot pts mid-move if institutional flow is genuine. Mean-reversion regime uses 3 pts = ~6 spot pts; if the deviation deepens by 6 spot pts beyond entry, the thesis is wrong and the move is accelerating rather than reverting. Per-bar arrays in code: trending=4, reverting=3.
exit.target_rationale: Trending regime: 7 option pts captures ~50% of expected 15-20 spot pt continuation burst from institutional TWAP flow at delta 0.5. Mean-reversion regime: 5 option pts captures the first ~10 spot pt snap-back from z-score extreme before the reversion stalls. Per-bar arrays: trending=7, reverting=5. Both give 1:1.5-1.75 R:R.

filters.vix_filter: none — VIX not used; regime is detected endogenously from NIFTY's own return structure
filters.time_filter: 09:20-15:25 IST; no entries after 15:20 to allow 90s time stop to run before EOD
filters.volume_filter: none at signal level — NIFTY index volume is aggregated and less meaningful than constituent volume
filters.trend_filter: endogenous — dir_consistency_36 acts as both regime classifier and trend filter
filters.spread_filter: not applicable — limit orders, no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — directional consistency is a proxy for HMM regime; as HFT participants become more prevalent, intraday microstructure regimes may become shorter-lived and harder to detect at 3-min windows

adaptation_notes: Major changes from original: (1) Full 3-state HMM with Viterbi/Baum-Welch fitting is infeasible at 5s frequency (computational cost, no stable fitting possible on intraday data); replaced with directional consistency (rolling sign autocorrelation proxy) which captures the same trending/mean-reverting/choppy distinction. (2) EMA periods compressed from 9/21 minutes (1-min bars) to 24/72 bars (2/6 min at 5s) — hold time compressed 15x (15-60 min → 30-90s) requires trigger signals at a faster timescale. (3) Bollinger Bands replaced with rolling z-score — cleaner measure for indexable price deviation without the BB width confound. (4) Previous-session HMM fitting requirement eliminated entirely — regime is detected in real-time from current session bars only. (5) Universe changed from NIFTY50 constituent stocks to NIFTY index itself — the regime-switching phenomenon applies more cleanly to the index because constituent-level noise is diversified away.
weaknesses: Directional consistency is a coarse HMM proxy — it cannot distinguish between a true trending regime and a temporary momentum spike; the full HMM's state probability confidence measure is absent

Both sub-strategies (trend + reversion) fire simultaneously on the same index, relying on the dir_consistency threshold to separate regimes; threshold miscalibration could result in entering the wrong sub-strategy
NIFTY trending micro-sessions driven by FII large orders may be less predictable post-algo fragmentation as orders split across venues
The 3-min regime detection window may lag genuine regime transitions; entry may occur at the tail end of a trend or the start of a new reversion

_source.original_target: STATE_1: 50 bps; STATE_2: revert to BB_mid
